headline: Vermont labor board remains below full strength as caseload grows
dek: The six-member panel has had vacancies for months while the number of cases it handles has increased, according to its executive director and VTDigger reporting.
body: The Vermont Labor Relations Board has been operating below its full six-member complement for months as its caseload has grown, VTDigger reported Sunday.

The board resolves disputes between workers and employers, oversees union elections, investigates unfair-labor-practice complaints and steps into contract negotiations when they reach an impasse. Its jurisdiction includes state workers as well as disputes involving schools, municipalities, colleges and private employers.

Executive Director Judith Dillon told VTDigger that the board received 62 cases in 2025, up from 48 in 2024. She also said the board held three days of hearings last year, compared with an average of 14 days over the previous decade.

The governor’s office said it was working to fill one of the two current vacancies and expected that appointment by the end of the following week. Vermont law calls for seats to be filled within 60 days of a vacancy from nominees recommended by a separate review panel. The governor’s office said the board has maintained a quorum and can continue its work while appointments are pending.
author: NorthEast News Desk
